name: Chlorhexidine / antibacterial body wash
summary: Hospital antiseptic wash used by some for body folliculitis; no trials for that use.
lead: Chlorhexidine is a cationic bisbiguanide antiseptic used on skin, wounds, in dentistry and on medical equipment, and it is available over the counter in the United States. Chlorhexidine washes are used in healthcare for Staphylococcus aureus decolonization, and some people use antibacterial body washes for body folliculitis.

name: Antibiotics (doxycycline) for back acne
summary: A prescription tetracycline antibiotic widely used for inflamed body acne; guidelines favour short courses alongside non-antibiotic treatments.
lead: Doxycycline is a synthetic, broad-spectrum antibiotic of the tetracycline class, developed by Pfizer and first marketed as Vibramycin in 1967. It treats a wide range of bacterial infections and is also prescribed for moderate to severe acne vulgaris.

name: Sunless tan / body makeup to hide marks
summary: Self-tanner and body makeup that visually blend stretch marks and scars; the effect is temporary and cosmetic.
lead: Sunless tanning and body makeup are cosmetic ways to visually mask uneven skin color, including stretch marks (striae) and scars, without a procedure. Sunless tanners darken the skin with a reactive ingredient, usually dihydroxyacetone (DHA), while bronzers and camouflage makeup apply removable pigment.

name: Dermablend / tattoo cover
summary: High-coverage camouflage makeup used to hide tattoos, scars and discoloration; effects are cosmetic and temporary.
lead: Tattoo cover products are camouflage makeups designed to conceal tattoos, scars, vitiligo patches, bruises and other skin irregularities with heavier coverage than everyday foundation. Dermablend is one commercial brand in this category.

name: Scar tattooing / micropigmentation
summary: Cosmetic tattooing that deposits pigment in scars or pale skin to blend them with surrounding skin; documented clinically but with little outcome data.
lead: Scar tattooing, also called micropigmentation, is a form of medical tattooing intended to hide a medical condition or the result of its treatment, typically in a realistic style. It is used to camouflage scars, reduce the visibility of vitiligo patches, and recreate areolas after mastectomy or chest surgery.

name: Stretch mark surgery / tummy tuck
summary: Abdominoplasty removes loose abdominal skin and tightens muscle; stretch marks on removed skin go with it, but it is major surgery with a notable complication rate.
lead: Abdominoplasty, commonly called a tummy tuck, is a surgical procedure that removes excess skin and fat from the abdomen and tightens the underlying muscle and fascia. It is typically sought after pregnancy or major weight loss, including after bariatric surgery, when loose skin and stretched abdominal muscles persist despite diet and exercise.

name: Slow bulking / slow growth to avoid stretch marks
summary: Gaining weight or muscle gradually in the belief that it lowers the chance of stretch marks; rapid growth is a recognised risk factor, but no trial has tested slow bulking.
lead: Slow bulking, or slow growth, refers to gaining weight or muscle gradually with the aim of avoiding stretch marks (striae). Stretch marks are dermal scars thought to be caused by rapid stretching of the skin.

name: Cellulite lasers / Cellfina
summary: Office procedures that cut or heat the bands behind cellulite dimples; one subcision device has 3-year follow-up data, but evidence for lasers is thinner.
lead: Cellulite lasers and Cellfina are in-office procedures aimed at the dimpled skin surface that many people, mostly women, notice on the thighs and buttocks. Cellfina is a tissue-stabilized, guided subcision device that mechanically releases the fibrous bands under the skin that are associated with dimple-type cellulite . Laser and other energy-based devices are a separate group of treatments that are discussed alongside it .

name: Body shaving / hair removal for skin texture
summary: Shaving or removing body hair to look smoother; a grooming choice with minor skin irritation risks and little dedicated research.
lead: Body shaving and hair removal, in this context, means removing chest, arm, leg or back hair to make skin look smoother or to show muscle definition. It is discussed in appearance communities as a style practice rather than a medical treatment. Men most often shave facial hair, and some also shave the chest, abdomen, underarms, legs or pubic area .

name: Brazilian tan / spray tan to even skin
summary: A DHA-based temporary skin color applied by spray to even out tone; lasts about a week and offers no UV protection.
lead: Spray tanning is a sunless tanning method in which a dihydroxyacetone (DHA) solution is applied to the skin to produce a temporary bronze color, used in appearance communities to even out skin tone. DHA reacts with amino acids in the dead outer skin layer rather than acting as a dye .

name: Estrogen/hormone skin theories (DHT acne)
summary: Forum theories tying acne to DHT, steroids and estrogen; androgens are linked to acne in dermatology, but looksmaxxing-specific claims lack dedicated studies.
lead: Hormone-and-skin theories in looksmaxxing communities center on the idea that androgens such as DHT, and drugs that change hormone levels such as anabolic steroids, drive acne, and that estrogen or anti-androgen approaches can offset it. Dermatology references do link androgens to acne: testosterone, DHT and DHEA increase sebum production, and DHT is described as the main hormonal driver of sebum .

name: Steroid back acne management
summary: Back acne that people link to steroid use; reference material is limited to general acne and androgen information.
lead: Steroid back acne (often called bacne in forums) refers to acne on the back and shoulders that people attribute to anabolic-androgenic steroid or testosterone use. Wikipedia states that anabolic-androgenic steroids and testosterone replacement can cause acne, and describes it as steroid acne .

name: Sliding genioplasty
summary: Cutting and moving the chin bone to reshape the chin; established surgery with case-series evidence and few comparative trials.
lead: Sliding genioplasty is a chin surgery in which a surgeon cuts the lower part of the chin bone and moves it forward, backward, vertically or sideways, then fixes it in place . Unlike an implant, it uses the patient's own bone.
claims: Sliding genioplasty can widen a narrow chin
Genioplasty can compensate for a poor bite or weak jaw

name: Gonial angle reduction (V-line surgery)
summary: Surgical shaving of the lower jaw angle (and sometimes chin) to narrow the lower face; established in East Asian aesthetic surgery, evidence is mostly surgeon case series.
lead: Gonial angle reduction, commonly marketed as V-line surgery, is a cosmetic jaw-contouring operation in which bone is removed from the angle of the mandible, where the lower border of the jaw meets the vertical ramus, in order to narrow the lower face and give it a tapered, V-shaped outline. It is frequently paired with reshaping of the chin.
claims: A narrower, V-tapered jaw is the more attractive lower-face shape
Botulinum toxin in the masseter can give a similar slimming effect without surgery

name: Custom PEEK/Medpor jaw implants
summary: Patient-specific implants designed from a CT scan to widen or lengthen the jaw and ramus; widely discussed online, with little published outcome data for purely cosmetic use.
lead: Custom jaw implants are patient-specific implants fabricated from a CT scan of the patient's facial skeleton to augment the jaw, typically at the gonial angle, the ramus, and sometimes the chin. Two materials are discussed most often in looksmaxxing communities: porous polyethylene, sold under the brand Medpor, and polyetheretherketone (PEEK), a rigid thermoplastic.
claims: A custom implant can give a more refined jaw than stock implants
The jaw should be designed to a target ratio such as bigonial to bizygomatic width
Implants can compensate for a jaw left undefined by previous surgery

name: Ramus / vertical ramus augmentation
summary: Adding height to the vertical part of the lower jaw, usually with a custom implant, for a longer and squarer jaw; essentially no published cosmetic outcome data.
lead: The mandibular ramus is the vertical portion of the lower jaw that connects the angle of the jaw to the joint near the ear. Ramus augmentation, or vertical ramus augmentation, refers to adding implant material along the ramus to increase its apparent height and the definition of the jaw angle, for a longer, squarer jawline.

name: Mandibular advancement surgery (BSSO)
summary: Established orthognathic operation that splits and moves the lower jaw forward; well studied for bite and function, and used by looksmaxxers to improve profile.
lead: Mandibular advancement by bilateral sagittal split osteotomy (BSSO) is an orthognathic operation in which the lower jaw is cut along the ramus on each side, split, and the tooth-bearing segment is moved forward and fixed in the new position. It is the most commonly described procedure for repositioning the mandible and is usually combined with orthodontic treatment.
claims: BSSO is a bigger improvement than genioplasty alone for a recessed lower third
An aggressive genioplasty can mimic a BSSO
BSSO carries a real risk of lasting numbness and relapse

name: FaceTite / Renuvion
summary: Subdermal radiofrequency (FaceTite) and helium-plasma (Renuvion) devices used to tighten the jawline and neck without a facelift; evidence is mostly case series, and the FDA has warned about off-label use.
lead: FaceTite and Renuvion are minimally invasive devices for tightening loose skin and contouring the lower face and neck. FaceTite, from InMode, delivers bipolar radiofrequency energy to the subdermal space through a small probe; Renuvion, which grew out of the J-Plasma system from Apyx Medical (formerly Bovie Medical), uses helium plasma energy to heat and contract subdermal soft tissue.

name: Morpheus8 (RF microneedling)
summary: InMode fractional radiofrequency microneedling device marketed for skin tightening and subdermal fat remodeling along the jawline and neck; evidence is mainly case series and reviews.
lead: Morpheus8 is a fractional radiofrequency microneedling device made by InMode that combines microneedles with bipolar RF energy to heat the dermis and subdermal tissue. Manufacturers and practitioners describe it as promoting collagen production, tightening skin and remodeling adipose tissue on the face, neck and body.

name: Hard-food diet (tough foods)
summary: Eating tough, fibrous foods to load the jaw; no human trial shows it changes jaw shape.
lead: The hard-food diet, also called tough-food chewing or "ancestral chewing", is a practice in which people deliberately eat fibrous or hard foods such as raw carrots, tough meats or similar items, with the aim of loading the jaw muscles and, in believers' accounts, improving jaw and facial development.

name: Jaw-chewing with Falim gum 8 hours
summary: Hard-gum chewing for hours to bulk the masseter; muscle growth is plausible, jaw pain is reported.
lead: Extended Falim chewing is a practice in looksmaxxing communities in which people chew Falim, a hard Turkish gum, for hours a day, in some accounts up to eight, to enlarge the masseter and widen or strengthen the lower face.
claims: Hours of Falim chewing widens and strengthens the jaw
Long chewing sessions can hurt the jaw joint

name: Chin strap while sleeping
summary: A strap to keep the mouth shut overnight; no evidence it reshapes the face.
lead: A chin strap worn during sleep is a band that holds the mouth closed overnight. In looksmaxxing communities it is discussed as a way to encourage nasal breathing and a closed-mouth resting posture, sometimes alongside mewing or mouth taping.

name: Myofunctional therapy
summary: Tongue and mouth exercises with sleep-apnea evidence; no evidence it changes facial looks.
lead: Orofacial myofunctional therapy (OMT) is a program of exercises for the tongue, lips, cheeks and throat muscles, used clinically for conditions such as obstructive sleep apnea, tongue dysfunction and open bite, and discussed in looksmaxxing communities in connection with tongue posture and jaw development.
claims: Myofunctional exercises can move a recessed jaw forward

name: Jaw contouring makeup (contour/highlight)
summary: Shading and highlighting to fake a sharper jawline; temporary and cosmetic.
lead: Jaw contouring is the use of makeup shading and highlighting to make the jawline look more defined. It applies the general technique of contouring, in which a shade darker than the skin creates apparent shadow and a lighter shade brings areas forward.

name: Neck tension / platysma flex
summary: Tensing the neck muscle for a sharper jaw-neck line in photos; a posing habit with no studies behind it.
lead: Neck tension or platysma flexing is a practice in looksmaxxing communities in which a person deliberately contracts the platysma, the thin superficial muscle of the neck, to make the jaw-neck transition and lower jawline look more defined, mostly for photographs or mirror checks.
claims: Flexing the platysma makes the jawline and neck look sharper.

name: Lower face rejuvenation filler (jowl filler)
summary: Filler placed along the pre-jowl and marionette lines to smooth the lower face; established aesthetic medicine with thin jowl-specific trial data.
lead: Jowl filler refers to injecting dermal filler into the pre-jowl, marionette and lower-face areas to restore lost volume and smooth the line of the jaw.

name: Jaw expansion via MSE / SARPE
summary: Surgical or mini-implant jaw widening for adults; real orthodontic procedures with documented complications, discussed in forums as a facial-width tool.
lead: SARPE (surgically assisted rapid palatal expansion) and MSE (miniscrew-assisted or maxillary skeletal expander) are ways of widening the upper jaw in adults whose palatal suture has fused. Looksmaxxing communities discuss them for facial width and bite, often alongside braces or bimaxillary surgery.
claims: SARPE can expand more than MSE, around 15 mm versus 12 mm.
Palatal expansion can change midface width and hollow cheeks.

name: Braces / orthodontics for jaw shape
summary: Established dental treatment for bite and tooth position that can change profile somewhat, especially combined with jaw surgery.
lead: Orthodontics is the dental specialty that diagnoses and corrects misaligned teeth, jaws and bite patterns, and can modify facial growth; braces are its best-known tool . In looksmaxxing communities it is discussed as a way to improve bite and facial profile, often alongside jaw surgery.

name: PRF / PRP face contouring
summary: Blood-derived concentrates injected for facial skin and volume; used in aesthetic clinics, with no trials of true contouring.
lead: PRF and PRP face contouring refers to using platelet-rich plasma or platelet-rich fibrin, concentrates made from a patient's own blood, to add volume or improve the skin of the face.

name: Tongue pressing against roof (tongue push-ups)
summary: A more forceful mewing variant; tongue presses on the palate, with no studies behind the facial-change claim.
lead: Tongue push-ups are a variant of mewing in which a person presses the tongue firmly against the roof of the mouth, sometimes in repeated holds, in the belief that this reshapes the jaws and face.
claims: Pressing the tongue hard against the palate reshapes the jaw and face.
